stories.title: Albany Plans $25M Makeover for Government Complex
stories.excerpt: New York’s Office of General Services (OGS) plans to spend $25 million to improve Empire State Plaza, a 98-acre complex of state government buildings in Albany, with the aim of creating a more active and accessible civic space. Detailed in a report prepared for OGS by architecture and design studio WXY, the plan draws on input from over 2,000 participants and envisions major enhancements to the complex, including green space, improved wayfinding and navigation, upgrades to the visitor experience in the Concourse and the Plaza, and improvements to the Swan Street and Madison Avenue gateways to the Plaza. The investment forms part of the $400 million Championing Albany’s Potential Initiative that Gov. Kathy Hochul launched last year in a bid to promote housing growth, attract new residents, and revitalize public spaces in New York’s capital city. OGS, the state’s real estate arm, oversaw the construction of the Plaza and has served as its caretaker since the complex was completed in 1978. The post Albany Plans $25M Makeover for Government Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NY OGS allocating $25M to Empire State Plaza improvements in Albany
Part of $400M Championing Albany's Potential Initiative targeting housing growth
Revitalization effort aims to attract new residents to state capital
stories.summary: New York's Office of General Services plans a $25 million makeover of the 98-acre Empire State Plaza in Albany, including green space, wayfinding, and gateway improvements. The project is embedded within Gov. Hochul's $400 million Championing Albany's Potential Initiative launched to spur housing growth and attract residents to the capital. The improvements target the Plaza's civic activation and visitor experience.
stories.impact: MINIMAL DIRECT RELEVANCE TO MULTIFAMILY DEVELOPMENT. While the initiative signals state support for Albany population growth, the $25M is for civic infrastructure, not housing supply or zoning reform. Watch for complementary housing policy changes or land disposition that would create actual multifamily development opportunity in Albany.

stories.title: New Apartment Building in Berkeley Heights Live-Work Campus Opens Doors
stories.excerpt: Move-ins are officially underway at RT500, a new 179-unit luxury community developed by The Connell Company in Berkeley Heights, NJ. The 11-story property is located within The Park, a 185-acre mixed-use campus about 30 minutes from downtown New York City. Greystar is managing leasing and in-person tours at RT500, which offers a mix of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartments. The Connell Company is touting the high-end amenities at the property, including a gym, co-working space, and dedicated game room. RT500 forms part of a $500 million redevelopment of a former office campus off Routes 78 and 22. In addition to the residential property, The Park also features a 176-room Embassy Suites Hotel, 1.5 million square feet of offices, and 160,000 square feet of dining, entertainment, wellness and lifestyle concepts. “From the moment residents walk through the doors, we want them to feel RT500 offers a place where their home, work, wellness, and social life can all come together,” said Shane Connell, executive vice president of The Connell Company in a statement. The post New Apartment Building in Berkeley Heights Live-Work Campus Opens Doors appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Connell Company delivered 179-unit RT500 in Berkeley Heights, NJ near NYC
Part of $500M mixed-use redevelopment (hotel, office, retail on 185 acres)
Live-work campus model with co-working, gym, positioning for white-collar proximity
stories.summary: RT500, a 179-unit luxury apartment community developed by The Connell Company, opened in Berkeley Heights, New Jersey, within The Park—a 185-acre mixed-use campus approximately 30 minutes from Manhattan. The 11-story property is part of a $500 million redevelopment of a former office park and includes co-working, gym, and lifestyle amenities. The property is managed by Greystar and offers studio through three-bedroom floor plans.
stories.impact: CONFIRMS SUBURBAN MULTIFAMILY DEMAND NORTH OF NYC DRIVEN BY LIVE-WORK MIGRATION. The live-work amenity package and near-completion timing signal sustained appetite for workforce housing within commuting distance of Manhattan, especially as hybrid work normalizes. Developers should track similar office-to-residential conversion opportunities on underutilized suburban campuses within 30–45 minutes of major metros.

stories.title: LaSalle IM, Camber Pick Up Long Island Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: A joint venture of LaSalle Investment Management and Camber Real Estate Partners has acquired a three-property industrial portfolio spanning more than 270,000 square feet on Long Island for an undisclosed price. The 100% leased portfolio includes a 46,000-square-foot facility in the JFK Airport area as well as two separate buildings measuring 100,230 square feet and 124,500 square feet in the South Shore area of Suffolk County, NY. “The portfolio provides a rare balance of credit-backed income stability and long-term asset strength,” noted Christopher Bellapianta, managing principal at Camber in a statement. “Its functional layout and prime infill locations position the portfolio to perform exceptionally well over time within a highly supply-constrained market.” The off-market transaction was arranged by a JLL Capital Markets Investment Sales team. LaSalle Investment Management, a subsidiary of JLL, manages $86.6 billion of assets globally. New Jersey-based Camber operates an 80-building, 4.5 million square foot portfolio, focused on value-add infill light-industrial properties in select East Coast markets. The post LaSalle IM, Camber Pick Up Long Island Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LaSalle IM + Camber JV acquired 270K+ SF industrial portfolio on Long Island
100% leased, includes JFK-adjacent and South Shore Suffolk County infill assets
Off-market deal signals strong institutional demand for supply-constrained East Coast logistics
stories.summary: A joint venture of LaSalle Investment Management and Camber Real Estate Partners acquired a three-property, 270,000+ square-foot industrial portfolio on Long Island, including a 46,000-square-foot facility near JFK Airport and two buildings totaling 224,730 square feet in South Shore Suffolk County. The portfolio is fully leased and positioned in supply-constrained infill locations. Camber operates 4.5 million square feet across 80 buildings focused on East Coast light-industrial value-add.
stories.impact: NOT DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO MULTIFAMILY. However, signals institutional capital flowing to supply-constrained logistics markets on Long Island; confirms tight industrial supply near NYC reinforces land scarcity across all real estate classes, potentially limiting multifamily development land availability and inflating land costs in the periphery. Monitor for competing capital flows that may drive up acquisition prices for multifamily sites in secondary submarkets.

stories.title: Related Companies Snags 150K-SF Lease at Upcoming Midtown Tower
stories.excerpt: Manhattan’s leasing frenzy continues, with global investment firm General Atlantic inking a long-term lease for more than 150,000 square feet at Related Cos.’ under-construction Midtown tower 625 Madison Ave. General Atlantic will occupy five floors as the anchor tenant upon the property’s opening, which is slated for 2029. The space will serve as the company’s global headquarters, supporting General Atlantic’s New York team of more than 330 professionals. Located between 58th and 59th Streets along Madison Ave., the 53-story tower designed by Foster + Partners will feature Central Park views, column-free floor plates and corners, and an all-electric and LEED Platinum design. A restaurant and luxury retail are planned for the tower’s base. Helmed by CEO Jeff Blau, Related has a portfolio of $100 billion assets owned or under development, including the Hudson Yards neighborhood on Manhattan’s West Side. The developer purchased the 625 Madison Ave. site in 2024 and demolished the existing 1956-vintage building, which had previously served as the headquarters for Nabisco and Related itself. The post Related Companies Snags 150K-SF Lease at Upcoming Midtown Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: General Atlantic signed 150K+ SF anchor lease at Related's 625 Madison Ave (Midtown)
53-story office tower opening 2029; General Atlantic HQ for 330+ NYC professionals
Reflects sustained corporate HQ demand in Manhattan despite remote-work trends
stories.summary: General Atlantic, a global investment firm, signed a long-term lease for more than 150,000 square feet across five floors at Related Companies' under-construction 625 Madison Ave tower, slated to open in 2029. The space will serve as General Atlantic's global headquarters for more than 330 professionals. The 53-story tower, designed by Foster + Partners, is LEED Platinum and all-electric.
stories.impact: SIGNALS SUSTAINED WHITE-COLLAR JOB ANCHORING IN MANHATTAN CORE. Major corporate HQ commitments to new Class-A office reinforce Manhattan as an agglomeration hub; this drives both direct worker in-migration and indirect service-sector employment growth, supporting multifamily demand in Manhattan and outer boroughs. Expect continued rent and occupancy strength for multifamily in Midtown South and Hudson Yards adjacencies through 2029–2031 ramp-up period.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges Refi for Van Nuys Warehouse Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Los Angeles Debt + Equity team, led by Zalmi Klyne and Stanley Chu, successfully arranged $6.1 million in permanent financing for three flex/showroom industrial properties located within the Los Angeles metro. Northmarq arranged financing on behalf of the borrower through a correspondent relationship with a life insurance company. The transaction was structured on a ten-year term. The portfolio included: 14943 Califa St. is a single-tenant industrial flex/showroom property built in 1955 and situated on a 0.33-acre site. The asset features a one-story design supporting a range of showroom, warehouse and light manufacturing uses. 15044 Keswick St. is a single-tenant industrial flex/showroom property built in 1969 and situated on a 1.48-acre site. 14932 Oxnard St. is a single-tenant industrial property situated on approximately 0.65 acres. Collectively, the three properties benefit from their locations in Van Nuys within the San Fernando Valley, one of Southern California’s most established infill industrial markets. The post Northmarq Arranges Refi for Van Nuys Warehouse Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northmarq arranged $6.1M refi for three Van Nuys flex/industrial properties
10-year permanent term from life insurance lender via correspondent relationship
Properties built 1955–1969; established San Fernando Valley infill industrial submarket
stories.summary: Northmarq's Los Angeles team arranged $6.1 million in permanent financing for three flex and light-industrial properties in Van Nuys (San Fernando Valley), totaling approximately 2.46 acres. The transaction was structured as a 10-year term funded through a life insurance company. The portfolio includes single-tenant showroom and warehouse uses built between 1955 and 1969.
stories.impact: NOT DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO MULTIFAMILY. Confirms San Fernando Valley as a persistent logistics/light-industrial market with refinancing activity; long-dated fixed-rate debt availability suggests stable cap-rate environment. Tangential note: Van Nuys industrial rents and land values may influence adjacent multifamily site costs if conversion/redevelopment activity emerges in the submarket.

stories.title: Westfield Montgomery Owner Pays Off $350M Loan on Bethesda, Md., Mall
stories.excerpt: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) has paid off a $350 million loan tied to the Westfield Montgomery shopping mall in Bethesda, Md., more than two years after the debt was transferred to special servicing. The 1.2 million-square-foot mall’s loan had been scheduled to mature Aug. 1, Bisnow reported. Morningstar Credit described the payoff as a “rarity in a cycle” in which many mall loans continue to receive extensions. URW secured the 10-year loan in 2014, with the debt tied to 836,000 square feet of the property. The mall received a two-year extension after missing its original August 2024 maturity date. French mall giant URW won approval in 2020 to redevelop Westfield Montgomery, but that project has not started. URW did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The payoff comes as URW has reversed course on its broader U.S. strategy. In 2022, the company said it planned to sell its $13.2 billion American portfolio, but last year opted instead to retain 11 high-performing flagship malls while continuing to unload non-core properties. Meanwhile, Westfield Montgomery has continued adding retailers and restaurants. The mall said in July that new arrivals throughout 2026 would include Pop Mart and Wetzel’s Pretzels, among others. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield paid off $350M loan on Westfield Montgomery mall
Loan had been in special servicing for 2+ years; payoff called 'rarity'
URW halted planned redevelopment; pivoting to retain flagships, divest non-core
stories.summary: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) paid off a $350 million loan tied to the 1.2 million-square-foot Westfield Montgomery mall in Bethesda, Maryland, more than two years after the debt was transferred to special servicing. The payoff was unexpected given the broader mall distress cycle; the loan had received a two-year extension after missing its August 2024 maturity. URW's planned redevelopment of the property has not commenced.
stories.impact: SIGNALS CONTINUED RETAIL REAL ESTATE STRESS AND DEVELOPER PORTFOLIO RESET. URW's retreat from U.S. mall redevelopment and focus on flagship retention suggests mixed-use opportunities (including residential conversion) at secondary malls like Westfield Montgomery may be delayed or shelved. For multifamily developers, monitor whether URW divests non-core malls to opportunistic buyers willing to pursue residential-anchored redevelopment; Bethesda's affluent submarket could support high-density residential if a new sponsor emerges.

stories.title: Vestal Point Capital Takes 12K SF at Rockrose Development’s 11 East 26th Street
stories.excerpt: Investment firm and hedge fund manager Vestal Point Capital is relocating its offices within New York City. The company has inked a long-term, 12,139-square-foot lease on the entire 12th floor of Rockrose Development’s 11 East 26th Street across the street from Manhattan’s Madison Square Park, Commercial Observer has learned. The company’s current address is listed on its website as 632 Broadway in NoHo. It is unclear when the firm will move. The exact length of the lease was unclear. The asking rent was more than $130 per square foot, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. Newmark‘s William Cohen and Ariel Harwood are the exclusive leasing agents for the property. Brian Goldman and Cooper Weisman — also from Newmark — represented the tenant in this deal. Newmark declined to comment, while a spokesperson for Vestal Point Capital did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Standing 21 stories tall, 11 East 26th Street is a two-building office complex connected to 15 East 26th Street. The second floor is a full-scale amenity club featuring a workout space, a private lounge, a designated area for whiskey lockers, and a grab-and-go kitchen. There is also a landscaped rooftop that includes terraces, seating areas, and an indoor-outdoor conference and entertainment space. Other tenants at 11 East 26th Street include artificial intelligence firm Sierra and business consulting firm Activate Consulting. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vestal Point Capital leased 12,139 SF (floor 12) at Rockrose's 11 East 26th St
Asking rent >$130/SF; relocation from NoHo (632 Broadway) to Flatiron area
Confirms continued Manhattan office demand from financial services/hedge fund tenants
stories.summary: Investment and hedge fund manager Vestal Point Capital signed a long-term lease for 12,139 square feet on the entire 12th floor of Rockrose Development's 11 East 26th Street, near Madison Square Park. The lease was negotiated at asking rents exceeding $130 per square foot. The firm is relocating from its NoHo headquarters at 632 Broadway.
stories.impact: CONFIRMS SELECTIVE OFFICE RECOVERY IN MANHATTAN'S FLATIRON/SOUTH MIDTOWN SUBMARKET. Professional services and financial tenants continue to consolidate and upgrade into high-amenity, newer buildings, signaling sustained white-collar employment and in-migration pressure in these neighborhoods. Supports multifamily demand in Flatiron and Union Square East adjacencies; watch for similar tenant flight from older NoHo/SoHo stock to fuel resi conversion opportunities.

stories.title: NYC Human Resources Administration Extends 174K-SF Lease in Midtown
stories.excerpt: The New York City Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) extended the lease for a government agency in Midtown South. The New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA) will get an extra 18 months at Vornado Realty Trust’s 260 11th Avenue, where it occupies 174,186 square feet, according to a source close to the deal. The deal appeared in a monthly Manhattan office market report by Colliers, which offered no further insight into the deal apart from the average office asking rent for Midtown South, which was $78.90 in August. DCAS negotiated the deal on behalf of HRA, but it’s unclear who brokered the deal for Vornado, which declined to comment. HRA’s lease was scheduled to turn over in October, The Real Deal reported in September 2022, and at some point it may have expanded its footprint from its initial 154,000 square feet. The agency has locations throughout the city, including a 350,000-square-foot office at Clipper Equities‘ 250 Livingston Street, where it offers legal services, and a 9,199-square-foot post at 25 Chapel Street in Downtown Brooklyn, where it provides assistance to veterans. Located between West 26th and West 27th streets several blocks south of Hudson Yards, 260 11th Avenue is a seven-story landmarked building constructed in 1911 and is known as the Otis Elevator Building. Vornado holds a 99-year ground lease for the property. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC HRA extended 174,186 SF lease at Vornado's 260 11th Ave for 18 months
Midtown South office market averaging $78.90/SF asking rent (Aug. data)
Government agency consolidating tenure amid broader Midtown South stabilization
stories.summary: The New York City Department of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) negotiated an 18-month lease extension for the Human Resources Administration (HRA) at Vornado Realty Trust's 260 11th Avenue in Midtown South, covering 174,186 square feet. The deal reflects broader Midtown South stabilization, with average asking rents at $78.90 per square foot as of August.
stories.impact: CONFIRMS GOVERNMENT TENANT RETENTION IN MIDTOWN SOUTH; SIGNALS STABILIZATION BUT NOT ACCELERATION. While the 18-month extension (rather than longer-term renewal) suggests caution, it indicates Vornado and DCAS expect near-term stability. For multifamily, government office tenancy anchors employment in Midtown South and Chelsea, supporting service-sector and transit-adjacent residential growth; however, the cautious lease term suggests no rush to ramp residential development in immediately adjacent markets.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Lends $310M for Jersey City Multifamily Tower Build
stories.excerpt: The demand for apartments across the Hudson River keeps rising. Namdar Group has landed $310 million of construction financing to build a 47-story multifamily tower in Jersey City, N.J., Commercial Observer has learned. Affinius Capital originated the loan for Namdar’s 1,049-unit Park Tower project in Jersey City’s Journal Square neighborhood. The large-scale development was given the green light by the Jersey City Planning Board in June a year after it secured a $32 million pre-development loan from Post Road Group paving the way for the tower, Jersey Digs previously reported. “Park Tower will be among Journal Square’s premier multifamily projects capitalizing on the neighborhood’s continued growth,” David Greenburg, co-head of debt origination at Affinius, said in a statement. “This project aligns with our strategy of financing exceptional multifamily assets with top-tier sponsorship.” Walker & Dunlop negotiated the debt with a capital markets institutional advisory team consisting of Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet and Edward Leboyer. Located at 8-16 Lott Street, the Park Tower project will have a mix of floor plans ranging from studios to three-bedroom units. Community amenities will include a fitness center, a yoga studio, a bowling alley, an arcade, a music room, a golf simulator and a rooftop lounge. Long Island-based Namdar Group has been an active developer in Jersey City, recently completing a 27-story, 564-unit luxury apartment tower at 35 Cottage Street in Journal Square. It also inked a $335 million debt package to refinance three newly built Jersey City multifamily properties totaling 833 units at 9 Homestead Place, 26 Van Reipen Avenue and 28 Cottage Street, as CO previously first reported. Namdar Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Namdar Group secured $310M construction financing from Affinius Capital for Park Tower
1,049-unit, 47-story multifamily tower in Jersey City Journal Square
Project approved June 2023; demonstrates sustained NYC-metro multifamily construction lending
stories.summary: Namdar Group landed $310 million in construction financing from Affinius Capital to build Park Tower, a 1,049-unit, 47-story multifamily development in Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The project received Planning Board approval in June 2023 and was preceded by a $32 million pre-development loan from Post Road Group. Walker & Dunlop negotiated the transaction.
stories.impact: STRONG SIGNAL OF CONSTRUCTION DEBT AVAILABILITY AND SUSTAINED SUBURBAN MULTIFAMILY DEMAND ACROSS HUDSON RIVER. Jersey City Journal Square continues to attract institutional debt for large-unit-count projects, indicating lender confidence in rent growth and absorption in the PATH-connected, high-transit-access submarket. Signals capital appetite for dense, transit-oriented multifamily in secondary metros; watch for similar funding for competing Jersey City projects and for debt-rate environment shifts that could throttle construction starts in Q1–Q2 2025.

stories.title: Industrious Adds 19th L.A.-Area Location at Caruso’s Masonic Temple
stories.excerpt: Coworking giant Industrious is adding another location in Southern California, this time at one of the more recognizable office properties in Glendale. The flexible office provider has signed for 12,000 square feet across two floors at Caruso’s historic Masonic Temple at 234 South Brand Boulevard, Commercial Observer can first report. The location is expected to open in late June 2027 as Industrious’ second in Glendale and 19th across Greater Los Angeles. It’s also Industrious’ first deal with Caruso. The new workspace will include 101 private office seats and 17 common-area seats. “Glendale has proven itself as a strong market for us, and we’re excited to build on that success with this new location,” Natalie Levine, director of real estate at Industrious, said in a statement. The nine-story Art Deco Masonic Temple was built in 1929, and Rick Caruso’s eponymous real estate company restored it as Class A office and retail space adjacent to the owner’s Americana at Brand shopping center. CBRE, which acquired Industrious last year, uses the property as its North L.A. headquarters. “Adding a premier flexible workplace within the historic Masonic Temple further strengthens the Americana at Brand’s live-work-play ecosystem, creating a seamless experience across one highly connected and walkable destination,” said Jackie Levy, chief revenue officer at Caruso. Industrious has been growing around Greater L.A. Earlier this year, the company opened an 18,400-square-foot location at Douglas Emmett’s Studio Plaza in Burbank, and signed a 22,000-square-foot deal at Sherman Oaks Galleria. The company also expanded aggressively across the Westside in recent years, including a 16,000-square-foot Beverly Hills location, roughly 44,000 square feet combined in Westwood and Santa Monica, and 19,000 square feet at Watt Plaza in Century City. Industrious operates more than 250 locations across more than 80 cities globally. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver
bullets: Industrious signed 12,000 SF lease at Caruso's Masonic Temple, Glendale
Flexible office provider's 19th LA-area location; opens late June 2027
Signals sustained demand for coworking/flex office in Southern California secondary markets
stories.summary: Coworking giant Industrious signed a 12,000-square-foot lease across two floors at Caruso's Masonic Temple (built 1929, renovated as Class A office) in Glendale, California. The location will be Industrious' second in Glendale and 19th across Greater Los Angeles, opening in late June 2027. The space will include 101 private office seats and 17 common-area seats.
stories.impact: NOT DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO MULTIFAMILY. However, Industrious' 19th LA location signals sustained flex-office demand and Caruso's willingness to co-tenant historic assets; tangentially, this reinforces Glendale as a secondary employment node, which over time may drive worker in-migration and multifamily demand. Monitor whether Caruso pursues residential or live-work components in future developments to capture workforce growth near coworking anchors.
